title: Quick Revision: Motion

table: Total length of the path covered (scalar)
Shortest distance from start to finish, with direction (vector)
Speed in a given direction (displacement per unit time)
Change in velocity per unit time
Equal distances in equal intervals of time

box: **Equations of motion (uniform acceleration):** v = u + at · s = ut + ½at^{2} · v^{2} − u^{2} = 2as
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time · Average velocity = (u + v)/2 (uniform acceleration only)
km/h → m/s: divide by 3.6 · Uniform circular motion: v = 2πr/t

bullets: Displacement can be zero even when distance is not (e.g. one full round of a track).
Distance–time graph: slope = speed. A straight sloping line means uniform speed.
Velocity–time graph: slope = acceleration; **area under the graph = displacement**.
A horizontal line on a velocity–time graph means uniform velocity (zero acceleration).
Uniform circular motion is **accelerated** motion: the speed is constant but the direction keeps changing.
Mixing km/h with m/s in the same formula. Convert first.
Forgetting the minus sign for retardation, or for a body thrown upwards (a = −g).

blocks.p: 1. A car speeds up from 18 km/h to 36 km/h in 5 s. Find its acceleration.
2. What does the area under a velocity–time graph tell you?
